summary: A short, self-guided craft and street-photo walk around Chang Moi Kao Road, where several established basket and rattan shops cluster near Chang Moi Road. Treat the famous hanging displays as working storefronts: browse, ask before photographing people or entering, and consider buying something if you use the shop as a portrait backdrop.
whyGo: Photograph layered woven goods, old shophouses and the contrast between long-running trades and newer cafés in the Chang Moi neighborhood.
Shop for handmade baskets, bags and homewares, then continue on foot toward Warorot Market or Tha Phae Gate.
bestFor: Street, craft and design photographers who enjoy observing a neighborhood at walking pace.
Visitors looking for practical woven souvenirs and willing to support local shops.
skipIf: You want a large artisan market, a guaranteed demonstration or a curated attraction with fixed hours.
You need a reliably step-free route or are uncomfortable walking beside city traffic.
duration: Allow 45–90 minutes for the shop cluster and nearby lanes; add time for shopping, a café stop or a walk through Warorot. This is a planning estimate.
cost: No admission is expected for walking public streets. Shop prices vary by item; no current reliable price list was found. Transport and purchases are extra.
hours: Chang Moi is a public neighborhood and can be walked any day. A travel feature updated in 2025 lists the basket shops it covers as daily, 09:00–17:30, while other local guidance describes independent workshops opening at different times. Treat those hours as indicative and confirm with a chosen shop shortly before visiting.
bestTime: Go in the morning for cooler walking and a better chance of finding shutters up. Soft morning light can bring out the texture of the woven displays; light and shade vary along the shopfronts.
gettingThere: Walk from Tha Phae Gate east toward Chang Moi Road and Chang Moi Kao Road, where the better-known wicker shops cluster; continue toward Warorot Market if you want to extend the walk. A resident-written 2026 Chang Moi guide estimates about 5 minutes from Tha Phae Gate to the district and 5–10 minutes onward to Warorot. From elsewhere, use a red songthaew, tuk-tuk or ride-hail to the Chang Moi Road junction, then walk. Times are approximate and traffic affects vehicle journeys.
booking: No ticket or reservation is needed for the street or shop browsing. For a particular store, check its current listing or contact it directly before making a special trip; no December 2026 holiday schedule was found.
accessibility: No formal accessibility details were located. Expect ordinary urban sidewalks, street crossings, uneven edges and possible goods displayed outside shops; shop interiors may be crowded or have raised thresholds. A continuous step-free route is not confirmed.
practicalTips: Start at the Chang Moi Road / Chang Moi Kao Road junction, browse the basket shops, then explore side lanes before walking on to Warorot. It is a small cluster rather than a full street of rattan stores.

Ask before photographing shopkeepers, customers, interiors or close details of a person's work. A storefront is someone's business, even when it is a popular photo location; accept a no and keep entrances clear.
Avoid blocking the sidewalk or handling merchandise without permission. If you make several photos using a shop as a backdrop, buy something or ask whether the owner is comfortable with it.
Carry small cash if you plan to buy; ask the price before choosing. Use a compact camera setup and watch traffic when framing shots from the road edge.
decemberNotes: December mornings are a comfortable planning choice, but no special photo event or confirmed 2026 year-end opening schedule was found. Individual shops may close or change hours around holidays; check shortly before going. The walk can be paired with Warorot, whose market hours should be checked separately.
uncertainties: The number of active rattan shops and their daily hours are not listed in a reliable official directory; a 2025 visitor guide reports daily 09:00–17:30 hours for its featured shops, but this may change.
No official photography policy, accessibility statement or December 2026 holiday schedule was found. Permission should be sought directly from each business and person photographed.
